tickets.title: US001: Exclusive .edu Account Registration
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want to register an account using only my valid '.edu' university email address, so that the marketplace remains exclusive to our campus community.

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Verify that the registration system accepts email addresses ending with the '.edu' domain.
- [ ] Verify that the system blocks registration attempts from public email domains (e.g., gmail.com, yahoo.com) and displays an error message.
- [ ] Verify that a verification link is sent to the provided '.edu' emai

tickets.title: US002: Enforced Safe Exchange Zone Selection
tickets.description:
As a Student, I want the app to force me to select a pre-defined Safe Exchange Zone before I can chat with a seller, so that our physical meetup on campus is safe.

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] Verify that when a buyer initiates a conversation, a mandatory popup forces them to select from a list of campus-approved Safe Exchange Zones (e.g., library lobby).

analysis.ambiguity1: The Student Union President states that the platform must be "exclusive" to people with a valid .edu email address. However, it is ambiguous because it does not specify whether this restriction applies only to account registration, or if it also restricts browsing items. Additionally, it remains unclear how the system should handle alumni or staff who also possess .edu emails but are no longer active students.
analysis.ambiguity2: A senior student requests the ability to "auction items" instead of just setting a fixed price. This is too vague to build because it lacks necessary functional metrics: it does not define the bidding rules, the minimum increment values, the auction duration limits, or how a winner is notified and bound to the transaction.
analysis.conflictSolution:
Conflict: The Student Union President wants to collect a 2% transaction fee to fund club activities , but the University Legal Team strictly forbids the app from processing payments or handling money directly, requiring students to pay via Venmo or cash.

Resolution: To comply with legal constraints, the app will remain completely cashless and will not integrate any payment gateway. To fund club activities, the Student Union can pivot to an alternative monetization model, such as charging a small flat subscription fee for "Premium Seller" accounts (students listing more than a set number of items per month) or charging external student organizations for banner advertisements within the app
analysis.nfr1: The system must restrict account creation strictly to authorized users with valid university domain credentials (.edu).
analysis.nfr2: The system must enforce physical safety protocols by requiring users to select an official, pre-defined 'Safe Exchange Zone' before opening a chat session.
analysis.nfr3: The mobile barcode scanning module must accurately process and decode book ISBN barcodes within a reasonable response time using the smartphone's built-in camera.
